note: All values are counts of English lemmas (dictionary headwords, inflections merged; derived words such as "effortless"/"effortlessly" count separately). Word-family sources were converted (see per-point "original"); approximate=true marks converted/interpolated points. Learner values count lemmas among the 5,000 most frequent only (X_Lex cap).

points.source: Meara & Milton (2003) via Milton (2010), Table 5: X_Lex < 1500 lemmas; value = rough midpoint (range is open at the bottom)
Meara & Milton (2003) via Milton (2010), Table 5: X_Lex 1500-2500
Meara & Milton (2003) via Milton (2010), Table 5: X_Lex 2750-3250 (Milton & Alexiou 2020 quote 2500-3250)
Meara & Milton (2003) via Milton (2010), Table 5: X_Lex 3250-3750
Meara & Milton (2003) via Milton (2010), Table 5: X_Lex 3750-4500

Meara & Milton (2003) via Milton (2010), Table 5: X_Lex 4500-5000. X_Lex is capped at 5000, so this is a floor; Nation (see Vocabulary and the CEFR, Victoria Univ.) suggests 7000-9000 word families for C2
Nation & Waring (1997): 4000-5000 word families at school entry, converted to lemmas x1.35 (approximate; original unit = word families)
Biemiller & Slonim (2001): ~8,400 root words by grade 5; Nation & Waring (1997) rule of 1000 families/year gives ~9,500; converted to lemmas x1.4 (approximate)

Interpolation, not a measurement: Nation & Waring (1997) 1000 families/year (~15,500 families at 16) with the lemma/family ratio rising from 1.4 (10k families) to 2.1 (Brysbaert 20-year-old: 42,000 lemmas vs ~20,000 families); approximate
Brysbaert, Stevens, Mandera & Keuleers (2016), Frontiers in Psychology 7:1116, Table 4: median 42,000 lemmas, 5th-95th percentile 27,100-51,700 (list of 61,800 lemmas; 11,100 base words)
Brysbaert et al. (2016), Table 4: median 48,200 lemmas, 5th-95th percentile 35,100-56,400

Brysbaert et al. (2016), Table 4: 95th percentile 51,700 lemmas (20-year-olds); 56,400 = 95th percentile of 60-year-olds. "Philosopher" has no measured basis; label attached to the best-supported high benchmark

Efron & Thisted (1976), Biometrika 63(3):435-447: 31,534 distinct word forms in his works (types, incl. inflections, probably names); converted to lemmas /1.7 (Brysbaert et al. 2016, types = 1.7 x lemmas) = ~18,500; they estimate he knew >= 66,500 types (~39,000 lemmas). Measures words USED, not known

calibration.description: Mean Pknown (share of respondents who know the word; Brysbaert, Mandera, McCormick & Keuleers 2019, BRM 51:467-479, ESM 2) for the lemmas of each 1000-rank band of en-freq.tsv (lemmas absent from their list, e.g. inflected forms kept as headwords, are skipped). Use it to compare the test to the average adult: expected known lemmas within the list = sum(bandSize * bandPrevalence).
calibration.caveat: Pknown is a population average over all respondents of that study (native/non-native mix and age spread not verified by me) and it is word-level, not person-level; treat as a rough yardstick.
